# Asymptotic Statistics {.unnumbered}

## Route to Chapter 25

Van der Vaart's preface Figure 0.1 shows two solid prerequisite routes into Chapter 25:

$$
2\longrightarrow6\longrightarrow7\longrightarrow8\longrightarrow25,
\qquad
2\longrightarrow18\longrightarrow19\longrightarrow25.
$$

In the preface caption, solid arrows mark prerequisites, dotted arrows mark natural continuations, and spatial position has no independent meaning. Figure 0.1 also contains solid source branches $2\to3$, $2\to5$, $2\to11$, $7\to15$, and $19\to20$, together with the dotted continuation $19\dashrightarrow5$. These chapters supply transformations, estimator construction, projection geometry, testing, and functional calculus that make Chapter 25 easier to verify even when Figure 0.1 does not draw a direct prerequisite arrow from them to Chapter 25. In the diagram below, **solid and gray-dotted arrows reproduce the included edges in Figure 0.1**; **blue dashed arrows are pedagogical bridges added by these notes**.

The chapter list retains the source order, while this diagram distinguishes source prerequisites from the notes' teaching connections. Within each chapter, the sidebar displays the numbered sections and explanatory subsections.

| Role | Linked route | What it contributes to Chapter 25 |

| Testing side branch | [Chapter 7](chapter-7.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 15](chapter-15.qmd), then the notes' bridge to [§25.6](chapter-25.qmd#sec-testing) | Gaussian testing, local power, and the efficient direction for a test |
| Source prerequisite: empirical processes | [Chapter 2](chapter-2.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 18](chapter-18.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 19](chapter-19.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 25](chapter-25.qmd) | Weak convergence of random functions, tightness, Donsker control, and infinite-dimensional estimating equations |
| Supporting estimator branch | [Chapter 2](chapter-2.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 5](chapter-5.qmd), with Figure 0.1's dotted continuation from [Chapter 19](chapter-19.qmd) | Consistency, Z-estimator linearization, estimated nuisance drift, one-step correction, and nuisance rates |
| Supporting projection branch | [Chapter 2](chapter-2.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 11](chapter-11.qmd) | Orthogonal projection, conditional expectation, residualization, and Hájek projection |
| Transformation branches | [Chapter 2](chapter-2.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 3](chapter-3.qmd), and [Chapter 19](chapter-19.qmd) $\rightarrow$ [Chapter 20](chapter-20.qmd) | Finite- and infinite-dimensional delta methods, von Mises calculus, and product-limit functionals |
| Semiparametric synthesis inside Chapter 25 | [geometry and lower bounds in §§25.2–25.7](chapter-25.qmd#banach-and-hilbert-spaces) $\rightarrow$ [estimating equations in §§25.8–25.9](chapter-25.qmd#sec-efficient-score-equations) $\rightarrow$ [likelihood constructions in §§25.10–25.12](chapter-25.qmd#sec-maximum-likelihood-estimators) | Turns the two prerequisite routes into tangent spaces, efficient influence functions, score operators, and estimators |

The two strands meet in Chapter 25: the first says what a regular procedure can achieve under local alternatives, while the second supplies the uniform stochastic control needed when the nuisance parameter is a function or distribution.

### Fast track to the main argument

For a first pass aimed specifically at Chapter 25, focus on:

1. [stochastic order, continuous mapping, and Slutsky](chapter-2.qmd#sec-stochastic-order), followed by the [finite-dimensional delta method](chapter-3.qmd#theorem-3-1);
2. [M- and Z-estimator construction](chapter-5.qmd#sec-m-z-estimators), especially estimated nuisance drift and one-step estimation;
3. [contiguity and Le Cam's third lemma](chapter-6.qmd#sec-contiguity), then [DQM, LAN, and local alternatives](chapter-7.qmd#sec-differentiability-quadratic-mean);
4. [Theorem 8.3](chapter-8.qmd#theorem-limit-experiment-reduction), the [convolution theorem](chapter-8.qmd#sec-convolution-theorem), and [local asymptotic minimaxity](chapter-8.qmd#sec-local-asymptotic-minimax);
5. [projection and conditional expectation](chapter-11.qmd#sec-projections), followed by the [Chapter 15 testing branch](chapter-15.qmd#sec-chapter-15-lan-power) before §25.6;
6. return to the infinite-dimensional route through [weak convergence of stochastic processes](chapter-18.qmd#theorem-weak-convergence-processes), [Donsker classes](chapter-19.qmd#donsker-classes), and the [functional delta method](chapter-20.qmd#theorem-20-8);
7. follow the Chapter 25 sequence [tangent spaces](chapter-25.qmd#tangent-spaces-and-information) $\rightarrow$ [efficient scores](chapter-25.qmd#efficient-score-functions) $\rightarrow$ [score operators](chapter-25.qmd#sec-semiparametric-score-operators) $\rightarrow$ [construction of efficient estimators](chapter-25.qmd#sec-efficient-score-equations).

Readers coming from modern machine learning or DML can follow the [modern-ML route through Chapter 25](chapter-25.qmd#sec-modern-ml-route), which connects tangent paths and influence-function construction to orthogonal, one-step, and cross-fitted estimators.

## Reading plan

- Week 1: [Chapter 2: Stochastic Convergence](chapter-2.qmd) and [Chapter 3: Delta Method](chapter-3.qmd)
- Week 2: [Chapter 5: M- and Z-Estimators](chapter-5.qmd)
- Week 3: [Chapter 6: Contiguity](chapter-6.qmd)
- Week 4: [Chapter 7: Local Asymptotic Normality](chapter-7.qmd)
- Week 5: [Chapter 8: Efficiency of Estimators](chapter-8.qmd)
- Week 6: [Chapter 11: Projections](chapter-11.qmd) and [Chapter 15: Efficiency of Tests](chapter-15.qmd)
- Week 7: [Chapter 18: Stochastic Convergence in Metric Spaces](chapter-18.qmd)
- Week 8: [Chapter 19: Empirical Processes](chapter-19.qmd) and [Chapter 20: Functional Delta Method](chapter-20.qmd)
- Week 9: [Chapter 25, §§25.1–25.7](chapter-25.qmd#semiparametric-models): geometry, bounds, testing, and transformed efficiency
- Week 10: [Chapter 25, §§25.8–25.9](chapter-25.qmd#sec-efficient-score-equations): efficient and general estimating equations
- Week 11: [Chapter 25, §§25.10–25.12](chapter-25.qmd#sec-maximum-likelihood-estimators): likelihood construction, least-favorable paths, and joint equations
